title: AtlasGrid x Redwood - Partner Discovery Call
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and AtlasGrid to explore reseller/technical integration for GPU cloud marketplace and dedicated capacity partnerships. Discussed infra compatibility (A100/H100, nvlink, RDMA), networking, billing models, benchmarking, pilot scope and next steps.
topics: hardware compatibility and networking (NVLink, InfiniBand, MIG)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 mins
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Ben Torres (AtlasGrid Partnerships), Priya Mehta (AtlasGrid Infra Lead), Daniel Kim (AtlasGrid Head of Product)

[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Laura from Redwood. Marcus is our solutions engineer. Ben, Priya, Daniel, thanks for making time. Do you want to do quick intros?
[00:12] Ben Torres: Yeah hi, Ben here, I run partnerships at AtlasGrid. We're a GPU cloud focused on enterprise workloads and partner marketplace listings.
[00:20] Priya Mehta: Priya, infra lead at AtlasGrid, we own the fleet and networking.
[00:24] Daniel Kim: Daniel, product. Nice to meet you all.
[00:28] Marcus Patel: Marcus, SE at Redwood. I work on performance and private deployment integrations.
[00:33] Laura Chen: Great — purpose here is a quick discovery; explore how we might support a go-to-market partnership, technical compatibility for Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments on AtlasGrid, and pilot ideas.

[00:45] Ben Torres: High level, we're interested in either listing Redwood as a managed inference provider in our marketplace, or doing a co-sell where we resell Redwood Dedicated capacity to our enterprise customers. We'd love to understand technical requirements and the integration surface.
[00:59] Laura Chen: Makes sense. Marcus, can you run through the typical integration patterns?

[01:05] Marcus Patel: Sure. There are a couple common models we see. One is marketplace listing: we provide a vetted image and deployment spec so customers can spin up Redwood endpoints on AtlasGrid with some automation. The other is Dedicated / reserved capacity where AtlasGrid would provide dedicated GPU pools for Redwood-managed inference for a customer — that requires network peering, possibly private control plane options, and some SSO/KMS integrations. There's also a hybrid where we run control plane in Redwood but data plane in AtlasGrid.

[01:40] Priya Mehta: On the infra side, our fleet is mixed A100 and H100 today, NVLink between some nodes, InfiniBand for RDMA. We also support MIG on A100 for multi-tenant workloads. Question is does Redwood support heterogenous fleets and can you fall back between A100/H100 models?

[01:58] Marcus Patel: Yes; our serving runtime supports model variants and routing policies. We can route by latency or cost and fallback to compatible model variants. For A100 vs H100 we do kernel selection and quantization profiles differently; we generally recommend H100 for high throughput but can run on A100. We do care about NVLink for large-model multi-gpu splits and RDMA for low-latency KV cache operations. Small caveat: some op kernels behave differently on H100 vs a100, so we'd want to validate with benchmarks.

[02:30] Daniel Kim: When you say "control plane in Redwood" what does that mean for customer data? We have customers asking about VPC options and whether traffic stays in their network.

[02:38] Laura Chen: Good callout. We have three deployment modes: hosted API (pure Redwood), Dedicated (reserved capacity with our management), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For Private we can offer a private control plane option where the control plane is customer-managed or in their VPC, and data doesn't egress. We also integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs.

[02:58] Priya Mehta: That sounds promising. For a marketplace listing, what pieces need to be published? Container images? Helm charts? Docs?

[03:05] Marcus Patel: Typically we provide a deployment manifest (Helm chart or k8s operator), a validated image, and a small operator that manages model artifacts, cache, and monitoring hooks. We also provide a benchmark harness so you can run a standard throughput/latency test per instance type.

[03:25] Ben Torres: On the commercial side, we're thinking about two models: revenue share for marketplace, or a committed monthly reserved capacity split where AtlasGrid gets a cut on the infra fee. Do you have standard terms or is this custom per partner?

[03:37] Laura Chen: We do both. Marketplace listing tends to be revenue share-based. Dedicated/resell is contract-based with committed capacity and pricing tiers. We can share a partner playbook and sample commercial terms.

[03:50] Daniel Kim: On the security side, customers ask for SOC2 and SSO. Do you have SOC2 and SAML/SSO integrations?

[03:57] Laura Chen: We're SOC2 Type II and support SSO/SAML and RBAC controls. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer IdP. We also provide encryption at rest and in transit and KMS integrations. We'll share the security pack.

[04:12] Priya Mehta: A couple technical specifics:
- network: we require at least 25Gbps NICs and recommend RDMA over InfiniBand for certain KV cache heavy workloads.
- kernel drivers: do you need specific drivers or CUDA versions?
[04:30] Marcus Patel: We recommend CUDA 12.x for H100 and 11.8+ for A100. For RDMA we use ibverbs. We'll supply exact OS/driver matrix. Also, if you want to run multi-gpu shards with NVLink we have recommended node shapes.

[04:50] Ben Torres: What's the typical pilot? How long, what metrics, and who owns benching?

[04:56] Marcus Patel: Pilots are usually 2-4 weeks for perf/compatibility + a week for a small production test. We supply a benchmark harness and baseline tests (throughput, p99 latency, token cost). We ask AtlasGrid to run the benchmarks on your instance types and share the logs; Marcus or our infra team will validate.

[05:16] Priya Mehta: We can run that but want a simple template.

[05:20] Marcus Patel: We'll send a runbook and a containerized harness — should be a few CLI commands.

[05:27] Ben Torres: Regarding billing integration if we list on our marketplace, we'd need metering hooks. Can Redwood emit usage events or invoices to our billing system?

[05:35] Laura Chen: We have usage webhooks and can send aggregated usage CSVs; for deeper marketplace billing we can integrate with your billing APIs. There's also the option of us invoicing AtlasGrid and you billing customers, or direct billing via the marketplace gateway.

[05:50] Daniel Kim: One more: data residency. Some enterprise customers require region locking. Does Redwood support region pinned deployments?

[05:57] Laura Chen: Yes — we support region pinning and can ensure models and data remain in-region. For Private we deploy inside the customer VPC/region.

[06:08] Priya Mehta: Great. On the infra risk side, do you have any special scheduling needs? Preemptible/spot instances?

[06:15] Marcus Patel: We can support spot/preemptible for non-critical workloads but for low-latency production SLOs we recommend reserved capacity. The runtime also supports graceful fallback to smaller models if preemptions occur. There's some config work around model sharding and checkpoint placement.

[06:34] Ben Torres: Any existing partners in a similar arrangement we can look at?

[06:38] Laura Chen: We have a few: StratusCloud and AuroraCompute have marketplace listings and dedicated pilots with Redwood. I can share their high-level case studies.

[06:50] Daniel Kim: Can we talk latency numbers? If a customer runs Redwood endpoints on our H100 nodes, what p99 should they expect for a 2k token generation on a 70B model?

[06:59] Marcus Patel: It's model-dependent. For a 70B on H100 with optimized kernels and NVLink multi-gpu, p99 could be in the 600-900ms range for streaming tokens, but it depends on quantization, batch size, and KV cache hit rates. On A100 it might be 10-20% higher. These are rough numbers; we'd need to bench your exact stack. Also note KV cache over RDMA reduces repeated prompt cost.

[07:28] Priya Mehta: We sometimes run MIG on A100 and want to sell smaller slices. Does Redwood work with MIG?

[07:34] Marcus Patel: We support MIG but with caveats: model sizes and throughput will be constrained, and not all kernels are MIG-friendly. For small models it's fine, but for large LLMs we prefer whole-GPU. We'll document recommended usage.

[07:48] Ben Torres: On SLAs, if we resell do you offer SLA credits or uptime guarantees?

[07:53] Laura Chen: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as part of contracts. For marketplace listings on partner infra we typically provide guidance but SLAs are jointly defined.

[08:05] Daniel Kim: Are there privacy or IP constraints for models? Can customers use their own models?

[08:11] Marcus Patel: Yes customers can bring their own models. We support model artifact management and version pinning. For certain regulated customers we can host models in their VPC/private deployment.

[08:22] Laura Chen: Great — this is heading towards a pilot. Proposed pilot: AtlasGrid runs our benchmark harness on one H100 and one A100 node (your standard instance shapes), we'll validate, then run a short Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool for a single customer. Thoughts?

[08:38] Ben Torres: Sounds good. Timeline wise we want to show something to internal stakeholders in 2-3 weeks. Is that feasible?

[08:44] Marcus Patel: Yes — if you run the harness this week we can validate in 3-5 business days and propose a pilot start the following week.

[08:53] Priya Mehta: We'll need the runbook and the expected driver/OS matrix.

[08:58] Marcus Patel: I'll share that. Also note some transcriptions folks get the product name wrong — we call it Redwood Dedicated (sometimes the automation labels it Redwood Dewicated in earlier docs) — small typos in older docs.

[09:12] Ben Torres: (laughs) good to know.

[09:15] Laura Chen: Okay let's recap and next steps.

[09:18] Laura Chen: Action items: 1) Marcus to send benchmark harness and OS/driver matrix; 2) Laura to share partner playbook and sample commercial terms; 3) Ben to share AtlasGrid instance types, regions, and internal stakeholder list; 4) schedule a technical deep dive week of 2026-05-25 with Priya and infra team.

[09:40] Daniel Kim: Quick question — do you have a standard partner onboarding doc?

[09:44] Laura Chen: Yes, I'll include onboarding checklist and a link to our security pack (SOC2, pen test summary).

[09:51] Ben Torres: We'll aim to run the harness by 2026-05-14.

[09:55] Laura Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with docs and a calendar invite for the deep dive.

[10:02] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-attributions and minor mis-phrasing (e.g., "NV link" vs NVLink, "KV cash").
